documentation.rationale: The identity and terms half is present: VIN (decode consistent), itemised out-the-door dealer price, and an Autotrader history summary (1 owner, no reported accidents). The maintenance half is absent: no service records, no transmission history, no recall closure, no photos of at-risk areas. The detail capture was incomplete, so the history entries and the gallery were not examined.

condition.rationale: Nothing wrong is stated or visible. The one examined photo shows clean, glossy red paint, an intact black soft top (folded) and unmarked 16-inch alloys. Nothing proves good condition either: gearbox, drains, leaks, tires and fluids are all unverified.

price_value.rationale: At $20,995 all-in dealer price, the car is about 5% under the tracker's fair-value mid of $22,163. That estimate mixes newer and higher trims. Against closer comps it sits at or above the band: the profile puts a 2017 Sport at about 25k miles at $17-20k in CA, a 2017 Sport with 24.8k sold at $19,500 in Napa, and a 2016 Club with 44k sold at $16,750. An early-2016 gearbox with no records, plus likely age catch-up, argues for the low side of that band.

mission_fit.rationale: Manual, light, reliable Japanese roadster near the ideal budget band, with easy resale in 6-24 months, so it fits the enthusiast bridge well. The early-2016 6MT question and the undocumented time-based maintenance stop it from being decisive until inspected.

logistics.rationale: California dealer 297 mi away. A CA smog certificate is included by law, and registration is straightforward. PPI access is not stated, but Orange County has many independent shops, so an inspection before money moves should be arrangeable.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Manual and apparently Soul Red, one of the profile's strongest colours, and it appears stock. It is the base Sport trim (no Club hardware) and an ND1 engine, so it is a typical example with one desirable trait in colour.

ppi_focus: 6MT on a warm car: 2nd/3rd synchro grind on quick shifts, any popping out of gear under load and overrun, and noises from the gearbox and differential.
Clutch: slip in 5th/6th at low rpm under load, engagement height, pedal squeak, hydraulic leaks at the slave cylinder.
Cabin water: lift the footwell carpets, check the soft-top drains behind the seats, and look for corrosion on the seat-rail bolts and floor connectors.
Soft-top fabric rub at the rear corners and header seal, and how the latch operates.
Oil seepage at the valve cover, front crank and timing-cover areas, and the rear diff pinion and output seals.
Water pump weep hole and coolant crust. Measure coolant and brake fluid condition.
Underbody skid plate and bracket (recall 19V496000) security. Look for signs of track or autocross use: tire shoulders, pad deposits, number-decal residue.
Paint meter for respray, nose and hood chips, and dents in the aluminium hood, trunk and fenders.
Tire DOT dates, battery test, alignment readings.
Mazda Connect screen for ghost touch or delamination; scan for stored codes.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a build date after the gearbox revision, or a documented Mazda warranty transmission replacement, plus a clean warm-shift PPI.
Up: dated invoices for brake fluid and fluids, recall closures confirmed, and recent tires by DOT code.
Up: the dealer negotiates toward the $18-19.5k band supported by the Napa 2017 Sport and the 2016 Club sales.
Down: grinding into 2nd/3rd when warm, clutch slip, wet carpet or corroded seat rails, or any branded title or undisclosed damage in the full report.
evidence.mission_note: A manual ND Miata in California squarely fits the enthusiast bridge brief: reliable, simple and easy to resell in 6-24 months. Its fit hinges on clearing the early-2016 6MT question and the missing time-based maintenance at a PPI.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity and terms well: VIN [VIN] decodes to a 2016 MX-5 Sport 2.0L, the 6-speed manual is stated, and the out-the-door dealer price of $20,995 is fully itemised. An Autotrader history summary reports one owner and no accident or damage; the report itself was not examined. Nothing is observed wrong. The single attached photo of this car shows clean red paint, a black soft top and unmarked factory 16-inch alloys. All maintenance evidence is open: no time-based service records, no transmission history or build-date photo on the 2016 6MT that the profile flags, no cabin-water or drain photos, and no tire or battery date codes. Two applicable recalls (19V496000 skid plate, 24V695000 airbag software) have no closure evidence. The detail page was not fully captured, so the remaining gallery and history entries are unknown rather than absent. On price, the car sits below the tracker's broad fair-value mid but at or above the profile's Sport band and the closest sold comps.
